![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14167856/assets/14b7f1e0ab3336feee7503ce45b289789a0a9ffc5e2ffbb035c71e8967a30048.png)

The line shown above passes through the points $(0,-2)$ and $(4,1).$ What is the equation of the line?
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,-2).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=-2.$

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(0,-2)$ and $(4,1),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-(-2)}{4-0} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=\frac{3}{4}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-2$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=\frac{3}{4}x-2
$$
